## A pioneer of IB programmes in Asia.
In 1997, UNIS Hanoi became the very first school in Asia to become an IB World School and offer all three IB programmes.
Students in Early Years 3 to Grade 5 follow the Primary Years Programme (PYP), while students in Grades 6-10 follow the Middle Years Programme (MYP) and students in Grades 11 to 12 undertake the IB Diploma Programme.
...
## An academically rigorous school.
At the start of 2020, a joint visiting Accreditation Team from the Council of International Schools, Western Association of Schools and Colleges and the International Baccalaureate Organisation concluded that UNIS Hanoi provides a robust academic programme connecting learning to authentic and meaningful real world experiences.

content.text:
There isn’t one universally “best” school—the right choice depends on your child’s age, preferred curriculum, budget, and where you live. These are strong options to consider:

| School | Best fit for | Curriculum / pathway |
|---|---|---|
| **United Nations International School of Hanoi (UNIS Hanoi)** | Families seeking a well-established, international community and a continuous IB pathway | IB PYP, MYP and Diploma Programme; ages roughly 3–18 |
| **British International School Hanoi (BIS Hanoi)** | Families who prefer a British-style education and a route to the IB Diploma | English National Curriculum, IGCSEs and IB Diploma; ages roughly 2–18 |
| **Concordia International School Hanoi** | Families seeking an American-style college-preparatory education | US curriculum with Advanced Placement courses; Preschool through Grade 12 |
| **Hanoi International School (HIS)** | Families wanting an IB school in a more central location | IB PYP, MYP and Diploma Programme |
| **St. Paul American School Hanoi** | Families looking for an American curriculum | American-style programme, with AP options |

**A quick way to narrow the list:**  
- Choose **UNIS** or **HIS** if you want an IB continuum.  
- Consider **BIS** if you want British schooling through IGCSEs, followed by the IB Diploma.  
- Consider **Concordia** or **St. Paul** for an American-style pathway.

Before applying, check each school’s current admissions availability, tuition and other fees, transport options, learning-support provision, and accreditation or programme authorisations. Visiting in person—and asking about the specific year group your child would join—can make the comparison much clearer.
